subject: zenGarden
pitch: A small Japanese garden diorama on a square base. A curved red wooden bridge over a koi pond with three orange and white koi, a stone lantern, a little pine tree with cloud-shaped foliage, a cherry tree in full pink blossom dropping petals, raked white gravel with a few mossy rocks, and stepping stones leading to the bridge.
reasoning:
I need a root joint at the origin since the builder requires one for parts to attach to, then I'm planning the diorama layout—a roughly 1x1.2 meter base with a small height budget for the scene elements like the cherry tree.

For the pond, I realize I can't carve a hole into the gravel slab, so instead I'm making it a raised water feature: gravel top, then a slightly elevated pond disc with a rim of small rock shapes around it, sitting just above the gravel surface.

I'm defining the pond as an extruded ellipse shape with teal water color, then adding koi fish on top using sphere-based bodies with painted orange and white patches, plus cone tails and fins, built as a reusable function so I can place several at different positions and rotations.

Working out the tail geometry using an extruded flat outline, computing the right and back direction vectors from yaw so the cross product gives the correct surface normal.

Now placing koi fish at various positions in the pond, each with slight y-offset and yaw rotation for natural variety.

For the bridge, I'm designing an arched deck spanning the pond from one gravel edge to the other, using a swept box section with a slight curve for the arch shape and defining the proper up-vector along the path.

Still writing bridge geometry...

I'm placing the bridge ends on the gravel base and setting the deck heights so they align properly. For the gravel I'm adding painted stripes for a raked texture, then defining the gravel slab as a thin box sitting just above the base layer.

I'm layering the pond geometry above the gravel so it sits slightly higher, with the koi positioned just above the water surface. Then I'm working out the wooden frame construction—a base box with a raised border lip around the edges to give the gravel tray a finished look.

Now I'm placing a ring of rocks around the pond's elliptical rim using scaled icosahedrons for a rough, natural look, skipping the areas near the bridge ends so the rocks don't overlap it.

I'm also laying out a path of flattened stepping-stone cylinders leading from the front-left toward the bridge's starting point, plotting their positions along a curved approach.

I'm finalizing the stepping stone path near the rim and now positioning a stone lantern toward the front right of the pond, checking its base against the pond's elliptical boundary.

I'm designing the lantern itself with hexagonal plinth, shaft, platform, firebox with glowing windows, a hexagonal cone roof, and a jewel finial, aiming for about 0.2 total height with mossy-gray stone coloring and warm yellow window accents.

For the pine tree, I'm sweeping a curved trunk with Catmull-Rom points tapering from thick to thin, then building cloud-style foliage pads from squashed spheres in varied greens stacked along the branches, with small bump spheres on top for texture.

Now I'm placing the cherry tree at the back right with a curved trunk growing taller, and giving it a pink blossom canopy made of ~14 flat-shaded icosahedron blobs scattered at random sizes using a soft pink color palette.

For falling petals, I'm scattering roughly 40 tiny box shapes (flattened to look like thin petals) with random rotations, some drifting in the air and others settled on the ground or floating on the pond, using a light pink color and keeping the total part count well under budget. I'm also planning four moss-covered rocks scattered across the gravel area at specific positions.

Now I'm sketching the garden builder setup, starting with a root joint at the origin before adding rocks, pines, and raked gravel stripes running along the z-axis.

Writing part placement code...

Still building koi parts...

Still writing bridge sweep logic...

Still shaping lantern geometry...

Still working out the pine tree's foliage pads and branch connections to the trunk sweep...

Now I'm laying out the second cherry tree: trunk points curving upward with tapering radii, then branches reaching up into a cluster of randomized blossom blobs squashed into an oval canopy shape.

Next I'm scattering 36 fallen petals around the tree base, varying their height depending on whether they land on ground or float on the pond's surface, with random rotations for natural scatter. The overall diorama stays compact with the tree height balanced against the base width, and now I'm starting on the stepping stone geometry.
